entry_state: Equipment cost, replacement, revaluation and employee-benefit examples preserve the history needed for later measurement. Impairment now introduces an asset floor that redirects a unit's loss rather than merely clipping it. The continuation must explain reversal ceilings and what happens when all admissible allocation capacity is exhausted.
exit_state: Impairment allocation preserves floors, depleted capacity and the no-impairment depreciation path. Production preserves normal-capacity evidence, cost populations and cash origins. Restoration then separates estimate changes, discount unwind and settlement, with cash classification still dependent on facts; the remaining changed-obligation and production cases follow.
findings: The requested CGU reversal of34 is limited to24, leaving PPE80 and no goodwill restoration. Zero-weight allocation remains explicitly unresolved.

Low, normal, high and idle production cases reconcile while retaining different variable spending. Adding all depreciation and subtracting full stock is consistent; mixing partial depreciation with full stock is wrong.
Restoration examples distinguish cost and revaluation models, exhausted assets and settlement. No new confirmed defect; remaining source/current-authority and zero-weight obligations are not closed.
